Hi Anita — thanks for the list. I pulled together the answers and an owner map below. I'll put Marissa and Kimberly on the thread for the detailed network diagram and the auditor attestation. Short answers first, then action items.

Short answers:
- Control plane callbacks (account management / license / console): we provide a set of regional static IPs; for US region customers the current published set is 3 IPs: 52.211.34.12, 52.211.34.13, 52.211.34.14 (TCP 443). These are used for control/control-plane only and are considered stable for the duration of the contract; any long-term changes are communicated 30 days ahead.
- Model inference egress: when running Redwood Private inside your VPC, inference requests to model shards happen within your network; however, if you choose to offload model shards to Redwood Dedicated or use the managed KV cache, you may see outbound connections to Redwood-managed NATs. Typical egress for managed services: 52.121.9.20 and 52.121.9.21 (TCP 443). If you need absolute pinning we can enable a dedicated egress NAT as a reserved capacity add-on.
- Ports & protocols: outbound 443 (TLS) is required for control plane telemetry and license checks. Health pings use TLS over 443 and occasional DNS lookups (UDP 53) to resolve internal endpoints.
- Evidence ownership: Redwood will provide a vendor-signed attestation document mapping our published IPs and the signed control-plane certificate thumbprint. Marissa will prepare the signed evidence package and Kimberly will coordinate the network diagram.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa Cole: prepare vendor attestation PDF (includes signed list of control-plane IPs + certificate thumbprint). Target: 2027-04-26 EOD.
- Kimberly Park: export final network diagram with NAT/egress path highlighted; mark any optional private relay / jump host patterns. Target: 2027-04-26 10:00 PT.
- Logan Wright: provide one-page summary for your auditors showing flow (control-plane vs optional managed egress) and the recommended firewall ruleset. Target: 2027-04-25 14:00 PT.

I'll attach the internal diagram we've been iterating on.

Cheers,
Logan
